policy: Every requirement below is bound to a verbatim excerpt from the SIRI page named in source_roles. Nothing is paraphrased into an excerpt and nothing is inferred. No excerpt text was typed: each is resolved from LINE NUMBERS out of a numbered dump by scripts/visa-registry/excerpts-from-lines.mjs, which fails the file unless both the display and lowercase forms occur literally in the normalized text.
structure_note:
This is the graduate-level Positive List, and it differs from the skilled-work list in three ways that matter.

THE EDUCATION IS PER JOB TITLE. Every title on the list carries its own required educational level, so 'I have a degree' is not the test — the degree has to match the level the list names for that title. The authority gives its own worked example (civil engineer, professional bachelor's minimum).

HOURS ARE 'USUAL', NOT A NUMBER. The skilled-work and Pay Limit routes state a floor in hours. This one requires that hours be usual for the field, normally 37 a week, with industry exceptions. A reader carrying the 30-hour figure across from the Pay Limit Scheme would apply a test this route does not use.

THERE IS NO EMPLOYER APPRENTICESHIP CONDITION. The skilled-work list requires the EMPLOYER to have met Læreplads-AUB training obligations, with no exemption possible. That condition does not appear here, and nothing is registered claiming it does.
freshness_note: No dateline. The body references 2028 in permit-duration examples and the list itself is revised on a published schedule, so a revision surfaces as a text change to the daily sync.
not_extracted: The list of job titles itself — several hundred occupations occupying lines 40 to 772 of the page, each with its required educational level. It is data rather than requirement, it is revised on a schedule, and a copy here would be stale while looking authoritative. The requirement that the job appear on the list IS extracted.
The criteria by which a job title is added to or removed from the list, which describe the authority's own list-making process rather than an applicant's obligations.
The step-by-step portal walkthrough, the document checklists, and the biometrics appointment procedure.
The rules for accompanying family members, which are a separate route.

requirements.label: The job must be included in the Positive List
A completed higher educational programme is required for every job title on the list
The required educational level is set per job title, not in general
requirements.description: Quoted with the authority's own worked example, because the general statement alone does not convey that the level varies.

requirements.label: Some job titles additionally require a Danish authorisation or official recognition
Salary and terms of employment must correspond to Danish standards
Working hours must be usual for the field — normally 37 hours a week
requirements.description: This route sets no numeric floor. Quoted whole, including the industry exception.

requirements.label: The offered salary must not be lower than normal in the field
Only liquid assets, labour-market pension payments and holiday allowance are taken into account
Housing, per diems, car, phone, internet, benefits-in-kind and subscriptions do not count
Salary must be paid into a Danish bank account in your own name
The Danish bank account must be opened within 180 days
A Danish authorisation is required for regulated professions, such as doctors
Documentation of the authorisation — or a receipt for having applied — must be attached
An accompanying family member must not have had a permit revoked more than once for lacking a work permit
A copy of the employment contract or job offer must be attached, stating all terms
Processing fee
Normal processing time, and the longer time if information is missing
One month before starting work — but only if you declare you can support yourself
Shorter employment gives a permit for its duration, plus an automatic 6-month job-seeking permit
You are not allowed to work during the job-seeking period
Four-year permit where the employment is four years or longer
A residence permit can only be valid until 3 months before the passport expires
The work permit is limited to the employment it was granted for
Losing the job revokes the permit
Apply for a job-seeking permit no later than two days after employment ends
Giving up your Danish address or staying abroad over 6 successive months lapses the permit
You must support yourself and may not receive benefits under the Active Social Policy Act
Biometric features must be recorded no later than 14 days after submitting the application
